meta.title: LingoLinq Capability Ledger
meta.purpose: Code-cited, present-tense source of truth for what the product actually does today, so compliance docs (and reviewers) ground claims against verified capabilities instead of re-deriving them by hand. citation-check.rb is to findings as capability-check.rb (Phase B) is to this ledger.
meta.canonicalWhen: Enforced as of Phase B: scripts/capability-check.rb validates every built/partial row's currentEvidence at HEAD and every deliberately-not-done row's negativeEvidence in CI (audit-artifacts-integrity). Mirroring to external tools (e.g. Codex AGENTS.md) is now permissible for these code-cited, identifier-free rows.

evidenceSemantics.currentEvidence: file:line:snippet that MUST resolve at HEAD (the current checkout), not a pinned SHA. Proves the capability is STILL true today. Required for status built/partial.
evidenceSemantics.introducedEvidence: optional provenance only (when/where a capability landed); NOT validated; may reference a historical SHA.
evidenceSemantics.negativeEvidence: scoped proof of absence for deliberately-not-done rows: grep scopes, patterns, excluded paths, reviewed surfaces, expectedMatches, and a re-review trigger. Phase B re-runs the greps at HEAD and fails if the match count diverges from expectedMatches.
evidenceSemantics.framing: deliberately-not-done rows describe out-of-scope-by-design choices, never known-gaps-shipped-without.

capabilities.capability: Password authentication (bcrypt-hashed, via the passwords concern / GoSecure)
capabilities.claimLanguage: Accounts are protected by password authentication with hashed credentials.
capabilities.notes: Password verification lives in app/models/concerns/passwords.rb; Google OAuth and SAML SSO also exist as alternative sign-in paths.

capabilities.claimLanguage: Two-factor authentication (TOTP) is available to users.
capabilities.antiClaim: NOT mandatory; do not claim enforced MFA for all users or admins.
capabilities.notes: Open item: make admin/staff 2FA mandatory (tracked separately). Optional today.

capabilities.capability: Server-side at-rest encryption of sensitive fields (secure_serialize / SECURE_ENCRYPTION_KEY)
capabilities.claimLanguage: Sensitive fields are encrypted at rest server-side.
capabilities.antiClaim: NOT end-to-end encryption; LingoLinq holds the keys. Do not claim 'zero readable keys' or E2EE.
capabilities.notes: Encryption keys are held by the application. This is server-side encryption, distinct from E2EE (see cap no-e2ee).

capabilities.capability: PiiScrubber pseudonymizes (scrubs direct identifiers from) payloads before AI egress
capabilities.claimLanguage: Only pseudonymized (scrubbed) data is sent to AI subprocessors; it remains personal data under GDPR/UK-GDPR.
capabilities.antiClaim: NOT de-identified or anonymized. Pseudonymized data is still personal data; does not meet HIPAA Safe Harbor.
capabilities.notes: Scrubber removes known direct identifiers (patterns + configured blocklist). NER coverage is an open limitation; free-hand third-party names can evade it.

capabilities.capability: COPPA hard-gate blocks AI generation for under-13 users awaiting parental consent
capabilities.claimLanguage: AI features are blocked for under-13 users until verifiable parental consent is captured.
capabilities.antiClaim: This is an under-13 (COPPA) gate; it does NOT itself enforce an EU under-16 (GDPR Art. 8) block on the AI path (see cap eu-under16-ai-block).
capabilities.notes: Gate is FeatureFlags.coppa_blocks_ai_for?(user); enforced at both AI generator call sites.

capabilities.capability: Jurisdiction detection primitive (EU vs non-EU) exists
capabilities.claimLanguage: The platform can determine whether an account context is in the EU.
capabilities.antiClaim: The EU jurisdiction primitive gates the Art. 50(1) disclosure modal (built and staged, gated OFF behind the article_50_disclosure flag; see cap art50-1-disclosure-modal) and, via the Phase 4 call-context helper, stamps jurisdiction on AiApiLog rows; it does not by itself drive an under-16 AI block.

introducedEvidence.note: lib/eu_jurisdiction.rb (module EuJurisdiction, line 12); PRs #556/#560. Consumed by LingoLinq::Article50CallContext.for at the three AI call sites (Phase 4, PR #635).

capabilities.notes: lib/eu_jurisdiction.rb states it gates the Art. 50(1) disclosure modal; fail-safe (only an authoritative non-EU result suppresses the modal). Phase 4 also uses it to stamp jurisdiction = 'EU' for the EU AiApiLog retention purge.

capabilities.capability: EU AI Act Article 50(2) machine-readable output marking -- board-generation slice only
capabilities.claimLanguage: AI board-generation output is marked in a machine-readable, server-verifiable way (Art. 50(2)).
capabilities.antiClaim: The Art. 50(2) obligation is NOT closed: this slice marks board generation ONLY. Other AI-output surfaces (generate_focus_words, AiWordPredictor.predict, eval narration, AiPredictionGenerator) are not yet marked, and durable persistence of the marker (board.settings + relinking copy_for) is follow-up. Also distinct from the Art. 50(1) disclosure modal (see cap art50-1-disclosure-modal).

currentEvidence.snippet: # EU AI Act Article 50(2): mark the board-generation output. The marking

capabilities.notes: Board-gen marking is unconditional (jurisdiction-independent). Remaining surfaces + durable persistence tracked as follow-up (see boards_controller#generate_labels).

capabilities.capability: Full hard-delete of a user on request (flush_user_completely)
capabilities.claimLanguage: Accounts can be permanently deleted on request.
capabilities.antiClaim: There is no automatic time-based wipe (no 48h/180d purge); deletion is on request / policy-driven.
capabilities.notes: Org-configurable retention exists via DataPolicyEnforcer; no NIST destruction certificates.

capabilities.capability: AiApiLog audit trail with scrubbed summary columns / IP redaction
capabilities.claimLanguage: AI API calls are logged with an audit trail and redacted of direct identifiers.
capabilities.antiClaim: Redaction is pseudonymization of the log record, not anonymization.
capabilities.notes: 90-day IP redaction runs as a scheduled job; EU AI Act fields present in schema.

capabilities.capability: AI board generation + word prediction via Anthropic Claude on AWS Bedrock (Anthropic-only runtime)
capabilities.claimLanguage: AI features (board generation and word prediction) use Anthropic Claude.
capabilities.antiClaim: The prior Google Gemini fallback was DISABLED 2026-07-09 (Gemini Developer/AI-Studio endpoint data-handling terms inadequate for child data); there is no runtime Gemini path today. Runtime AI egresses to Claude on AWS Bedrock (the Bedrock Mantle Messages API via lib/ai_client.rb), not the direct api.anthropic.com endpoint; enforced in CI by scripts/ai-endpoint-guard.sh. Only pseudonymized data is sent (see cap pii-scrubber-pseudonymization).

introducedEvidence.note: Bedrock routing switch (lib/ai_client.rb, AiClient.build) recorded in docs/legal/AWS_BAA_ACCEPTED.md + docs/legal/ANTHROPIC_BAA_ACCEPTED.md 2026-07-24; Gemini fallback removal in docs/legal/AI_DATA_SHARING_CONSENT.md section 2.2 and docs/legal/AI_GOVERNANCE_MEMO.md

capabilities.notes: Runtime constructs the sanctioned Claude client via AiClient.build (Bedrock Mantle); no direct Anthropic client or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY read on the runtime seams (CI guard scripts/ai-endpoint-guard.sh). Subprocessors listed in docs/legal/SUBPROCESSORS.md; that register's Gemini row may need a runtime-status update to reflect the 2026-07-09 disable (flagged separately, not fixed here).

capabilities.capability: Message banking retains the user's OWN voice recordings for playback
capabilities.claimLanguage: Message banking stores a user's own recorded messages for playback.
capabilities.antiClaim: These are the user's own communication recordings, NOT voiceprints/speaker-ID/biometrics (see cap no-voiceprints).
capabilities.notes: Most sensitive data category (health-adjacent, ALS use). A temp WAV made only for auto-transcribing a text label is deleted; the banked recording is retained by design.

capabilities.capability: Signed AWS Business Associate Agreement (HIPAA-eligible AWS services in use)
capabilities.claimLanguage: A signed BAA is in place with AWS covering HIPAA-eligible services in use under the BAA'd account, including S3 storage and Amazon Bedrock runtime AI inference.
capabilities.antiClaim: The AWS BAA does NOT cover a direct third-party model endpoint outside AWS (e.g. api.anthropic.com). That direct path is unused at runtime today; when used it is covered by the Anthropic HIPAA-Ready BAA (see cap anthropic-model-provider-baa). Fable/Mythos models are excluded from Bedrock HIPAA eligibility.
capabilities.notes: AWS BAA signed 2026-02-07 (account 2390-4478-5114). Bedrock runtime routing recorded 2026-07-24. Attestation-type evidence (document, not code).

capabilities.capability: EU AI Act Article 50(1) user-facing AI-interaction disclosure modal
capabilities.claimLanguage: An accessible EU-gated AI-interaction disclosure modal, an acknowledgement endpoint, and a shared first-AI-use gate are built and staged.
capabilities.antiClaim: Built and staged, but gated OFF: the `article_50_disclosure` frontend flag is registered in AVAILABLE_FRONTEND_FEATURES only (not enabled for any user), so the modal is shown to no one yet. Do not claim a LIVE or enabled Art. 50(1) disclosure in production. Enabling the flag is the 2026-08-02 release gate, on Scot's sign-off, after the production deploy.

introducedEvidence.note: Modal + ack endpoint + first-AI-use gate: PR #646 (Phase 3). Flag registered AVAILABLE-only: Art50 Phase 5 (RLL-01), lib/feature_flags.rb article_50_disclosure.

capabilities.notes: Disclosure content (lib/lingo_linq/ai_consent_disclosures.rb, Phase 2), Ember modal + ack endpoint + gate (Phase 3), and jurisdiction stamping (Phase 4, cap jurisdiction-primitive) are all built and on staging. Inert until the flag is enabled. EU clock 2026-08-02.

capabilities.capability: Jurisdiction-aware under-16 (EU GDPR Art. 8) block on the AI generation path
capabilities.claimLanguage: AI features are blocked for EU users aged 16 and under until a parent grants EU AI parental consent via the email-token flow.
capabilities.antiClaim: This gate is NOT the same as signup COPPA (settings['coppa']) or second-tier AI data-sharing VPC (settings['ai_consent'] / government-ID). It only covers EU under-16 AI enablement.
capabilities.notes: Persists registration country + under_16/eu_under_16; prefs AI section gated; email-token settings['eu_ai_parental_consent']; folded into ai_feature_enabled_for? with call-site defense.

capabilities.antiClaim: We do NOT do E2EE. Encryption is server-side with LingoLinq holding keys (see cap encryption-at-rest-serverside).
capabilities.notes: The #1 recurring over-claim in Gemini-drafted docs.

capabilities.capability: Zero-data-retention (ZDR) confirmed for the two active Anthropic models
capabilities.claimLanguage: The Anthropic models used at runtime (Claude Haiku 4.5 for board suggestions/prediction, Claude Opus 4.7 for eval narration) are ZDR-confirmed per Anthropic's data-retention documentation (verified 2026-07-06).
capabilities.antiClaim: ZDR is confirmed ONLY for these two specific models; it does NOT extend to any other/future Anthropic model outside the ZDR-eligible tier, and NOT to any non-Anthropic provider. ZDR is NOT a substitute for a HIPAA BAA (see cap anthropic-model-provider-baa for the executed Anthropic BAA and cap aws-s3-baa for Bedrock under the AWS BAA). Fable 5 / Mythos-class models are explicitly NOT ZDR-eligible and never receive identifiable payloads.
capabilities.notes: Confirmed against Anthropic Privacy Center data-retention documentation, not a bespoke signed ZDR addendum. Reverify on any runtime model change.

capabilities.capability: Voiceprints / speaker-identification / voice-cloning of training audio
capabilities.antiClaim: We do NOT process biometric voiceprints or perform speaker-ID. Message banking stores the user's own recordings (see cap message-banking-own-voice).

negativeEvidence.reviewTriggers: any change under app/models/button_sound.rb adding audio identity/cloning, or a new speaker_* column

capabilities.notes: Voice cloning is import-only (built externally, finished voice imported) per 2026-06-24 decision; no training recordings handled.

capabilities.capability: Diagnosis / disability / IEP / 504 / medical-condition data fields
capabilities.antiClaim: We do NOT collect diagnosis/disability/IEP/504/medical fields. AAC use is not a disability proxy (UDL/special-ed/gen-ed/ESL all use AAC).

negativeEvidence.reviewTriggers: any migration adding a health/disability/diagnosis/IEP column

capabilities.notes: Art. 9 special-category data arises only from free-text content a user/supervisor stores, not from a structured field.

capabilities.capability: Signed BAA covering the AI model-provider (Anthropic) egress path
capabilities.claimLanguage: A signed Anthropic HIPAA-Ready BAA covers the Anthropic model-provider path; active runtime AI uses Claude on AWS Bedrock under the AWS account BAA instead.
capabilities.antiClaim: Google (Gemini) as a model provider still has no BAA; its runtime fallback remains disabled (2026-07-09). The Anthropic BAA is the still-available direct-path basis, not the active Bedrock route.
capabilities.notes: Supersedes the former deliberately-not-done cap no-model-provider-baa. Anthropic HIPAA-Ready BAA executed 2026-07-18; runtime moved to Bedrock 2026-07-24 under the AWS BAA. Id retained as anthropic-model-provider-baa so inbound references to the closed gap resolve. Operative conditions verified 2026-07-27: the deployed Cloud Run service lingolinq-web signs Bedrock with a credential that resolves to the BAA'd AWS account 2390-4478-5114 (us-west-2), and Bedrock model-invocation logging is OFF in that account/region (residual: shared app AWS credential, not a dedicated Bedrock credential).
